title: Cream Cheese
description: Prepared with cream, rennet, and milk.

ingredients.name: a small tub of fresh morning's milk
cream skimmed from an equal quantity of last evening's milk

steps: Add the cream skimmed from an equal quantity of last evening's milk to a small tub of fresh morning's milk
Mix the cream and the new milk together, and warm them to about blood-heat or 100 degrees of the thermometer
Have ready a cup of water in which has been soaking, since last night, a piece of rennet (the salt wiped off), about the length and breadth of two fingers
Stir the rennet-water into the vessel of mixed milk and cream, and set it in a warm place till the curd has completely formed
With a knife, cut the curd into squares
Take a large, thin, straining-cloth, and press it down on the curd so as to make the whey rise up through it
As the whey rises, dip it off with a saucer or skimming dish
When the whey is nearly all out, put the curd into the cloth, and squeeze and press it with your hands till it becomes dry
Crumble the curd very fine with your hands, and then salt it to your taste
Wash the straining-cloth clean, and lay it in the cheese-hoop
Put the crumbled curd into the cloth, and then fold the rest of the cloth closely over it
Set the cheese-hoop on a clean wooden bench or table
Place on it its round wooden cover so as to fit exactly, and lay on the top two bricks or a heavy stone
After it has stood six hours in the hoop or mould, turn it, and let it stand six hours longer
When you take out the cheese, rub it all over with a little fresh butter
Set it in a dark, dry place, turning it every day
In four or five days it will be fit for use

steps: Hogs should be well fattened on corn for about eight weeks, allowing ten bushels to each hog.

title: East India Pickle
description: Prepared with cabbage, cauliflower, and cucumbers.
steps: Have ready a small white cabbage sliced with the stalk removed; a cauliflower cut into neat branches; sliced cucumbers; sliced carrots; sliced beets nicked round the edges; button-onions; string-beans; radish pods; barberries; cherries; green grapes; nasturtians; capsicums; bell-peppers, &c.
Sprinkle all these things with salt, put them promiscuously into a large earthen pan, and pour scalding salt and water over them
Let them lie in the brine for four days, turning them all over every day
Take them out, wash each thing separately in vinegar, and wipe them carefully in a cloth
Lay them on sieves before the fire, and dry them thoroughly

To every two quarts of the best vinegar, put an ounce and a half of white ginger root scraped and sliced; the same of long pepper; two ounces of peeled shalots or little button-onions, cut in pieces; half an ounce of peeled garlic; an ounce of turmeric; and two ounces of mustard seed bruised, or of mustard powder
Let all these ingredients mixed with the vinegar infuse in a close jar for a week, setting in a warm place, or by the fire
Put the vegetables all into one large stone jar, or into smaller jars, and strain the pickle over them, keeping them well covered with liquid
Put a table-spoonful of sweet oil on the top of each jar, and secure them well with a large cork and a leather
If the vegetables have absorbed the liquor, prepare some more seasoned vinegar and pour it over them

title: East India Pickle
description: Prepared with cucumbers, onions, and beans.

ingredients.name: one ounce of turmeric to the gallon
a quarter of a pound of white race ginger
half a pound of white mustard seed
half a pint of small red peppers
quarter of a pound of grated horse-radish
half a pint of flour mustard

steps: Lay in strong brine for two weeks, or until convenient to use them, small cucumbers, very small common white onions, snap beans, gherkins, hard white cabbage quartered, plums, peaches, pears, lemons, green tomatoes and anything else you may wish
When ready, take them out of the brine and simmer in pure water until tender enough to stick a straw through
If still too salt, soak in clear water
Drain thoroughly and lay them in vinegar in which is dissolved one ounce of turmeric to the gallon

For five gallons of pickle, take two ounces of mace, two of cloves, two of cinnamon, two of allspice, two of celery seed, a quarter of a pound of white race ginger craked fine, half a pound of white mustard seed, half a pint of small red peppers, quarter of a pound of grated horse-radish, half a pint of flour mustard, two ounces of turmeric, half a pint of garlic if you like and soak in two gallons of cider vinegar for two weeks, stirring daily
After the pickles have lain in the turmeric vinegar for a week, take them out and put in jars or casks, one layer of pickle and one of spice out of the vinegar, till all is used
If the turmeric vinegar is still good and strong, add it and the spiced vinegar
If the turmeric vinegar be much diluted do not use it, but add enough fresh to the spiced to cover the pickles
Put it on the fire with a pound of brown sugar to each gallon
When boiling, pour over the pickle
Repeat this two or three times as your taste may direct
